# nofollow

*Directive* · also written rel=nofollow

A rule, on a whole page or on one link (rel=nofollow), that asks Google not to follow links; Google treats it as a hint.

**Glossary** (*nofollow*): A hint not to follow links or pass signals through them; as a page-level robots rule it covers every link on the page. It does not block crawling.

10 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 6 shown or said at the event (1 not in Google docs, 2 confirmed by Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Qualify your outbound links to Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/qualify-outbound-links), [Evolving "nofollow" – new ways to identify the nature of links](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2019/09/evolving-nofollow-new-ways-to-identify), [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag).

- [`D1-C101`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Docs: Google's faceted navigation guide prefers prevention: disallow filter URLs in robots.txt and keep crawlable only item pages plus one unfiltered listing page, or use URL fragments, which Google generally does not crawl. rel=canonical and nofollow are weaker, slower options. `[D1-C101, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/faceted-navigation]`
- [`D1-C127`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Docs: Google treats nofollow as a hint for crawling, not a block: nofollow links will generally not be followed, but the linked pages may still be crawled if Google finds them through sitemaps or other links. To stop Google fetching URLs on your own site, use a robots.txt disallow rule. `[D1-C127, docs, Google Search Central, Search Central blog (10 September 2019), https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/qualify-outbound-links]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C066`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: John Mueller said AI crawlers do not really know what to do with nofollow links, because they look at the content rather than building a link graph; he did not say whether he meant Google's AI systems, other AI crawlers or both. `[D2-C066, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C107`](../sessions/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) Slide, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: The nofollow rule can still consume crawl budget: Google does not crawl through the nofollow link itself, but it still crawls the linked page when it finds that page through other links. `[D1-C107, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C068`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The robots rule none is equivalent to noindex plus nofollow, so a page that carries it will not show up in Search, provided Google can see the tag. `[D2-C068, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C063`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The page-level nofollow robots rule tells search engines not to pass signals to any of the links on the page, which John Mueller called a weird and very broad rule that makes the page stand on its own. `[D2-C063, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C064`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: John Mueller recommends rel=nofollow on individual links instead of the page-level nofollow robots rule, so a site can choose which links are useful and which are not. `[D2-C064, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C821`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: John Mueller suspected that if robots meta tags were reinvented today, the page-level nofollow rule would probably not be part of them. `[D2-C821, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C065`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: Audit robots meta tags set by templates and plug-ins: an explicit all rule does nothing and can go, while a page-level nofollow strips link signals from every link on the page and is better replaced by qualifying only the specific links that need it. `[D2-C065, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C067`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: nofollow is a link-graph hint for search engines, not an access control: to keep AI crawlers away from content, use robots.txt rules for the specific crawlers; at Google, Google-Extended covers Gemini training and grounding, and the Search generative AI control covers AI Overviews and AI Mode. `[D2-C067, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-IDX-02` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not use noindex, nofollow or crawl-delay to save crawl budget (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IDX-06` **SHOULD** · Documented: Prefer rel attributes on individual links to a page-level nofollow (5 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
